## Channel Consent

Whether a channel may be used to reach someone — email, SMS, phone, post, push, in-app.

```ts
import { ChannelConsentField } from '@cardstack/catalog/fields/consent/consent-vocabulary';

@field channels = containsMany(ChannelConsentField);
```

### Separate from Consent Grant because the two fail independently

Permission to market to someone (the **purpose**) says nothing about whether their email address still works (the **channel**). An address that hard-bounced is unusable no matter what they agreed to, and someone who withdrew marketing consent may still have a perfectly good address for service messages.

This is the modelling error the whole family is built to avoid.

### Suppression is not withdrawal

The distinction that matters most here.

| | What it means | Can it be fixed? |
|---|---|---|
| **Withdrawal** | the person said no | only by them saying yes again |
| **Suppression** | delivery failed or was blocked | often — a new address, a delisting |

`SuppressionReasonField`: hard bounce · spam complaint · do-not-contact list · invalid address · manual.

Collapsing suppression into withdrawal does two kinds of damage: it **loses the ability to re-engage** someone who simply changed their address, and it **overstates how many people opted out** — a metric organisations make decisions on.

### Double opt-in is recorded, not assumed

`doubleOptInConfirmedAt` is separate from `optedInAt`. **A signup that was never confirmed is pending, not consented.** Systems that treat the two as the same send to addresses nobody ever confirmed owning — which is how a typo'd address receives someone else's mail.

`requiresDoubleOptIn` is per-channel because the requirement varies by channel and jurisdiction; `isConfirmed` reads it rather than assuming.

### `blockedReason` orders the causes by what the reader can act on

Suppression first — it is the one they cannot fix by asking again.

### Non-goals

Does not store the address itself. Does not send anything. Does not decide whether a send is allowed; the consumer's send path reads this field and Consent Grant together.
